request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Small requested changes expanded into rewrites.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Compare the work with the request before responding.",
    "description": "Use for tasks.",
    "name": "scope-check"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "A skill can guide scope management."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":2,"justification":"The body only says to \"compare the work with the request\" without specifying what to check for, what counts as scope overrun, or what corrective action to take, so it gives no concrete behavioral change."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"Both the description (\"Use for tasks.\") and body are generic platitudes that could apply to any task at all, providing no specific guardrail against the scope-expansion failure mode."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Use for tasks.\" is not a real Use-when trigger — it fails to name the condition (e.g., small/targeted change requests) that should activate this skill, so it would fire indiscriminately or never reliably."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence-specific details — it is fully generic (if uselessly so)."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"A one-line generic reminder to check scope is not complex or reusable enough to warrant a skill; a feedback-memory rule or a concrete checklist step would be a cheaper and more effective vehicle for this correction."}}

actionability.justification: The body only says to "compare the work with the request" without specifying what to check for, what counts as scope overrun, or what corrective action to take, so it gives no concrete behavioral change.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: Both the description ("Use for tasks.") and body are generic platitudes that could apply to any task at all, providing no specific guardrail against the scope-expansion failure mode.

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns, file names, or evidence-specific details — it is fully generic (if uselessly so).

routing_fitness.justification: A one-line generic reminder to check scope is not complex or reusable enough to warrant a skill; a feedback-memory rule or a concrete checklist step would be a cheaper and more effective vehicle for this correction.

trigger_quality.justification: "Use for tasks." is not a real Use-when trigger — it fails to name the condition (e.g., small/targeted change requests) that should activate this skill, so it would fire indiscriminately or never reliably.
